Lessons.Title: Fitting Lines
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: compare candidate fit lines by residuals, calculate a least-squares regression line using legitimate technology when available and interpret fitted slope/intercept. Independently authored Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition U03:L05, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/3/5/preparation.html (CC BY 4.0). The source includes an actual scatter-plot card sort and technology-assisted least-squares fit; a manual calculation is explicitly a substitute, not evidence that a calculator was used.

Original hypothetical data: (x,y)=(0,2),(1,4),(2,7),(3,9). The x mean is1.5, y mean5.5. Sum[(x−1.5)(y−5.5)]=12 and sum[(x−1.5)²]=5, giving regression slope12/5=2.4 and intercept5.5−2.4×1.5=1.9. Thus least-squares model is y=2.4x+1.9.

Predictions from fitted line are1.9,4.3,6.7,9.1 and residuals observed minus predicted are +0.1,−0.3,+0.3,−0.1. Squared residual sum=.01+.09+.09+.01=.20. For a plausible simpler line y=2x+2, predictions2,4,6,8 yield residuals0,0,1,1 and squared residual sum2. The least-squares fit is better under this specified criterion.

Student task: rank two lines by residual totals, use actual software if available to confirm least-squares coefficients, critique an outlier's effect and explain that line choice is based on an objective such as squared-error minimum. Teacher-scored rubric 0–2 each for correct fit arithmetic, two compared residual series, interpretation of model and actual or transparently simulated technology use.

KeyConcepts.Title: Least-squares line
KeyConcepts.Definition: Line minimizing sum of squared vertical residuals in a linear regression.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use data pairs and an explicit residual definition.
KeyConcepts.Example: For four original points, fitted y=2.4x+1.9.

KeyConcepts.Title: Residual sum of squares
KeyConcepts.Rule: Compare models using same observations and units.
KeyConcepts.Example: Fit SSE=.20 vs simple line SSE=2.

KeyConcepts.Title: Interpret coefficients
KeyConcepts.Definition: Slope and intercept describe model change and initial prediction.
KeyConcepts.Example: Slope2.4 output units per x unit.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Comparing fit using absolute errors while claiming least squares
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Different criteria can rank models differently.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Specify sum of squared vertical residuals.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Claiming software-generated regression from hand calculations
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Authored calculations do not show a real software interaction.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Document actual technology use or label as independent computation.

SummaryPoints: Fit lines are compared against the same scatter observations.
Least squares minimizes squared vertical residuals.
This sample's fitted line y=2.4x+1.9 yields SSE .20.
Teacher checks reasoning, regression software evidence and model interpretation.
